title: How React works through the update queue

slides.say: When you call a setter, React does not update right away. It adds the update to a queue.
Two kinds of entries. A value, like zero plus five, means replace with five. A function means run this updater.
After the handler finishes, React re-renders and works through the queue in order.

steps.say: Replace with five ignores the old value. The result is five.
The updater gets that five and returns six.
React stores six and returns it from use state.

slides.text: Updaters run during rendering, so they must be pure. No side effects inside.
slides.say: Updater functions run during rendering. So keep them pure: just return the next value.
